name: Nasturtium
grown_as: A tender annual flower, edible in leaf, flower and seed, sown in spring. Trailing and climbing kinds, and compact 'Tom Thumb' bush kinds. Colour varies from yellow to orange to deep red by variety: drawn orange. ⚠️ CHECK
habit: Trailing or scrambling stems to 1 to 3 m, climbing by twisting leaf stalks; compact kinds a mound 30 cm. Succulent, smooth, hairless, slightly peppery-smelling.

leaf.type: Simple, shield-shaped (peltate): the stalk joins the underside near the middle, not at the edge
leaf.outline: Round, 5 to 15 cm across, sometimes slightly angular
leaf.base: None: the leaf is a round disc with the stalk underneath, slightly off-centre
leaf.margin: Entire, gently wavy, sometimes with shallow blunt points where the veins end
leaf.veins: Eight or nine pale veins radiating from the stalk point like the spokes of a wheel, forking near the edge
leaf.surface: Smooth, hairless, slightly waxy so water rolls off in beads; paler beneath
leaf.stalk: Long (5 to 20 cm), fleshy, joining the centre of the leaf beneath

flower.form: A broad open trumpet with a long straight spur sticking out behind
flower.petals: Five, free: the upper two broad, rounded and marked with dark lines; the lower three narrower with fringed, hairy claws at their base
flower.colour: Orange (also yellow, red or cream), the throat with darker red streaks
flower.centre: Eight stamens around a three-lobed style, half hidden in the throat
flower.behind: Five coloured sepals, the upper one drawn out into a nectar spur 2 to 3 cm long
flower.carried: Singly on long stalks from the leaf joints, held level or facing out among or above the leaves

fruit: Three rounded, ridged and wrinkled seeds joined in a cluster, green, turning pale buff and corky as they dry, about 1 cm each. Seed: a single wrinkled, ridged, roughly round segment, pale brown.
seedling: The seed leaves stay in the seed in the soil. The first leaves above ground are already small round shields on long stalks.
winter: Nothing: killed by the first frost, self-sown seeds sprouting the next spring

leaf: a round shield-shaped leaf with the stalk joining underneath near the centre
eight or nine veins radiating like wheel spokes
bloom: five orange petals, the upper two broad, the lower three with fringed bases
seed: a wrinkled, ridged, roughly round seed
seedling: small round shield leaves on long stalks
young: round shield leaves on long stalks
flower: orange spurred flowers held among the leaves
round shield leaves on long stalks

look_alikes: Pennywort (navelwort, Umbilicus rupestris) has small fleshy round leaves with the stalk in the middle, but grows in walls and has spikes of tiny greenish bells. Canary creeper (Tropaeolum peregrinum) has lobed leaves and small fringed yellow flowers.
